# Karman

> Karman Corporate Services Pte Ltd (UEN 202012889R) is a Singapore corporate services firm and ACRA Registered Filing Agent. It helps founders and fund managers incorporate and run Singapore companies and Variable Capital Companies (VCCs): incorporation, nominee director, corporate secretary, accounting and tax, GST, and Employment Pass support.

Office: 60 Paya Lebar Road #06-28, Paya Lebar Square, Singapore 409051. Phone: +65 8074 3630. Email: team@karman.com.sg.

Content on this site is general information, not legal or tax advice. Each guide shows its last-updated date; figures reflect Singapore rules as of that date.

## Services
- [Accounting & Bookkeeping Services Singapore](https://karman.com.sg/services/accounting): Outsource accounting for your Singapore small business. Monthly bookkeeping, financial statements, Singapore business tax filing (ECI, Form C-S), and GST returns. Fixed monthly fees.
- [Singapore Company Incorporation 2026](https://karman.com.sg/services/company-incorporation): Register a company in Singapore ACRA-registered filing agent for local and foreign founders. We handle your Singapore company incorporation form end-to-end. Same-day submission, 48-hour approval.
- [Corporate Secretary Singapore - Company Secretary](https://karman.com.sg/services/corporate-secretary): Appoint a corporate secretary for your Singapore company. Annual Return filing, AGM, director changes, share transfers. ACRA-registered. Startups welcome.
- [GST Registration Singapore - Register & File](https://karman.com.sg/services/gst-registration): GST registration and quarterly filing for Singapore companies. Compulsory threshold S$1M, voluntary registration available. End-to-end service by Karman.
- [Nominee Director Singapore for Foreign Founders](https://karman.com.sg/services/nominee-director): Professional nominee director for Singapore Pte Ltd companies. Satisfies ACRA's resident director rule. Fully documented with NDA and indemnity deed.
- [VCC Fund Administration Singapore - VCC Setup](https://karman.com.sg/services/vcc-fund-administration): Set up a Singapore Variable Capital Company (VCC) with Karman. MAS-regulated fund structures for PE, hedge funds, and family offices. Includes 13O/13U tax incentive filing and full fund administration.

## Guides: Company incorporation & structure
- [Why ACRA Rejects Company Incorporations (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/acra-company-incorporation-rejected-reasons): ACRA rarely rejects a well-prepared application.
- [ACRA Nominee Director Changes 2026: What Every Foreign Founder Must Know](https://karman.com.sg/blog/acra-nominee-director-changes-2026): Nominee directors remain fully legal in Singapore, but since June 2025 they must be arranged through an ACRA-registered Corporate Service Provider, filed on ACRA's central nominee registers (ROND and RONS), and their nominee status is visible on the public business profile.
- [Why AI Startups Are Incorporating in Singapore in 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/ai-startups-incorporating-singapore-2026): AI startups choose Singapore for strong IP protection, clear and sandbox-friendly regulation, deep-tech grants, an active venture capital ecosystem, and access to Southeast Asia's 700 million consumers - plus a corporate tax regime with startup exemptions.
- [Apostille & Legalisation of Foreign Company Documents for Singapore (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/apostille-legalization-foreign-company-documents-singapore): Foreign company documents used in Singapore must be authenticated.
- [Best Singapore Incorporation Services (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/best-company-incorporation-services-singapore): The best Singapore incorporation service is an ACRA Registered Filing Agent that includes the government fee, constitution, registered office and post-incorporation documents, and offers reliable corporate secretary and compliance support for the years after incorporation.
- [Can a Foreigner Start a Business in Singapore?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/can-foreigner-start-business-singapore): Yes.
- [Cost to Incorporate a Company in Singapore (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/cost-of-incorporating-company-singapore): Incorporating a Singapore company involves a fixed, modest ACRA government fee plus a filing agent's service fee.
- [Dropshipping Business Registration Singapore: Complete 2026 Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/dropshipping-business-registration-singapore): You can dropship in Singapore without a company, but IRAS taxes the profits either way.
- [ESOP in Singapore Pte Ltd: Complete Founder's Guide (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/esop-singapore-pte-ltd-guide): A Singapore Pte Ltd can grant employee share options without being listed or getting MAS approval.
- [How Long Does Singapore Company Incorporation Take? (2026 Timeline)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/how-long-does-singapore-company-incorporation-take): ACRA usually approves a standard Singapore company within 1-3 business days, sometimes within hours, once documents are complete.
- [Incorporate a Company in Singapore as a Foreigner](https://karman.com.sg/blog/how-to-incorporate-company-singapore-foreigner): A foreigner can incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd fully online through an ACRA Registered Filing Agent, often within one business day.
- [How to Start a Business in Singapore: Complete 2026 Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/how-to-start-business-singapore-2026): To start a business in Singapore, choose a structure (usually a Pte Ltd), register with ACRA through BizFile+ via a filing agent, appoint a resident director and company secretary, open a corporate bank account, and register for tax.
- [Nominee Director Singapore - Everything You Need to Know (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/nominee-director-singapore-complete-guide): A nominee director is a Singapore-resident individual appointed to meet the Companies Act requirement for at least one locally resident director.
- [Paid-Up Capital Singapore: How Much Do You Need? (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/paid-up-capital-singapore-company): A Singapore Pte Ltd can be incorporated with as little as one share issued for one dollar, with no deposit required before incorporation.
- [How to Redomicile Your Company to Singapore: 2026 Legal Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/redomicile-company-to-singapore): There are three ways to move a business to Singapore: inward redomiciliation under the Companies Act (since 2019, only from jurisdictions that allow outward transfer), incorporating a new Singapore Pte Ltd and transferring the business, or a share-swap flip.
- [Singapore Bank Account for Foreign Company: Complete Guide 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-bank-account-foreign-company): Foreign-owned Singapore companies can open a corporate bank account with traditional banks such as DBS, OCBC and UOB, which often require an in-person meeting and stricter KYC, or with digital providers such as Aspire and Airwallex, which open fully online.
- [Singapore Incorporation for Australian Founders](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-australian-founders): Australian founders can incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd remotely with a nominee director and keep their Australian Pty Ltd running in parallel.
- [Singapore Incorporation for Chinese & HK Founders](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-chinese-hongkong-founders): Chinese and Hong Kong founders can incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd remotely with a nominee director, using Singapore as a neutral, English-law-based base with 90-plus tax treaties.
- [Singapore Company Incorporation for Foreign Founders: 2026 Data Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-foreign-founders-2026): In 2026, Singapore remains a leading headquarters choice for foreign founders: 100% foreign ownership, a 17% headline tax rate with startup exemptions, 100+ tax treaties and incorporation in 1-3 days.
- [Singapore Incorporation for Indonesian Founders](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-indonesian-founders): Indonesian founders typically incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd as a holding company over an Indonesian PT, which regional VCs prefer for fundraising.
- [How to Incorporate a Singapore Company as a Malaysian Founder (2026 Guide)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-malaysian-founders): Malaysian founders do not need to relocate to incorporate in Singapore - a nominee director meets the resident director rule.
- [Singapore Incorporation for UK Founders (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-uk-founders): UK founders can incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd remotely with a nominee director, benefiting from English common law, the UK-Singapore FTA and a full double tax agreement.
- [Singapore Company Incorporation for Vietnamese Founders (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-vietnamese-founders): Vietnamese founders usually incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd as a holding company over their Vietnamese entity or as a standalone international company.
- [Singapore Company Setup for Marketplace Sellers (Amazon, Shopee, Lazada, TikTok Shop)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-marketplace-seller-company-setup): Marketplace sellers on Amazon, Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop benefit from a Singapore Pte Ltd: business seller accounts, multi-currency banking, limited liability and startup tax exemptions.
- [Setting Up a Regional HQ in Singapore: EDB Incentives & Tax Benefits 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-regional-headquarters-setup): A Singapore regional headquarters is a Singapore Pte Ltd that manages a group's Asia-Pacific operations.
- [SAFE & Convertible Notes for Singapore Pte Ltd: Founder's Guide (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-safe-convertible-note-guide): Singapore Pte Ltds can raise early money through SAFEs (a right to future equity) or convertible notes (a loan that converts).
- [Singapore Startup Ecosystem 2026: Grants, VC, Accelerators & Why Founders Choose Singapore](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-startup-ecosystem-2026): Singapore has produced more than 25 unicorns, ranks first in Southeast Asia for startup ecosystems according to Startup Genome 2024, and attracts US$4-5 billion in venture capital each year.
- [Grants for Singapore Startups: Complete 2026 Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-startup-grants-guide): Singapore's main startup grants include Startup SG Founder for first-time founders, the Enterprise Development Grant, the Productivity Solutions Grant, Market Readiness Assistance, Startup SG Tech and Startup SG Equity.

## Guides: Tax
- [Singapore Budget 2027 Public Consultation: How Businesses Can Give Feedback by 6 January, and What Founders Should Ask For](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-budget-2027-business-feedback): MOF consultation 12 Nov 2026 to 6 Jan 2027, submission channels, the three themes, and the CIT rebate, grant and work pass issues founders should raise.
- [Singapore Withholding Tax on Payments to Foreign Companies (2026): Rates, Treaty Table and Examples](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-withholding-tax-foreign-companies-guide): Domestic rates (15% interest, 10% royalties, 17% onsite services, 0% dividends), treaty rates by country, the remote-services exemption, IR37 deadlines and worked examples.
- [OECD Pillar Two and Singapore: What It Means for Your Holding Company](https://karman.com.sg/blog/oecd-pillar-two-singapore-holding-company): OECD Pillar Two imposes a 15% minimum tax only on multinational groups with annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more.
- [Singapore Budget 2026: Corporate Tax Rebate, AI Deductions Explained](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-budget-2026-corporate-tax): Singapore Budget 2026 gives every active company a 50% corporate income tax rebate for YA 2026, capped at S$40,000, and expands the Enterprise Innovation Scheme with up to 400% deductions on qualifying AI and R&D spending.
- [Singapore Corporate Tax Guide for Small Businesses (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-corporate-tax-guide-small-business): Singapore charges a flat 17% corporate tax, but new companies pay far less: under the startup tax exemption the effective rate is about 6% on the first S$200,000 of chargeable income for the first three years.
- [Setting Up a Holding Company in Singapore for Gulf Assets](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-holding-company-gulf-assets): Gulf investors use Singapore holding companies for cross-border assets because Singapore offers one of the deepest tax treaty networks in the world, no capital gains tax, the foreign-sourced income exemption under Section 13(8), and a credible legal system.
- [Singapore Holding Company: Tax Benefits, DTA Network & Structure Guide 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-holding-company-tax-benefits-guide): A Singapore holding company offers no capital gains tax on share disposals, no withholding tax on outbound dividends, a 17% headline rate with partial exemptions, the foreign-sourced income exemption, and 100+ tax treaties.
- [Singapore Startup Tax Exemption (SUTE): How It Works in 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-startup-tax-exemption): The Singapore Startup Tax Exemption (SUTE) exempts 75% of the first S$100,000 and 50% of the next S$100,000 of chargeable income for a new company's first three Years of Assessment, giving an effective rate of about 6% on the first S$200,000.

## Guides: Compliance & filings
- [Why Singapore Keeps Appearing in the Nvidia Chip Story, and What It Means for Trading Companies](https://karman.com.sg/blog/nvidia-megaspeed-singapore-export-controls-trading-companies): Nvidia's billing-location revenue change, MHA's Megaspeed and Alice Huang findings, AI server fraud charges, Singapore's export-control position and a compliance checklist for trading companies.
- [ACRA Changes from 20 October 2026: What Every Singapore Director Must Do](https://karman.com.sg/blog/acra-changes-october-2026-what-directors-must-do): New annual return confirmations, a CEO question, no more registered office opening hours, and faster striking off.
- [Singapore Company Year-End Checklist 2026: 10 Deadlines and Rule Changes Before 2027](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-year-end-checklist-2026): Form C-S due 30 Nov, the CIT cash grant appeal deadline, the new S$6,000 EP salary floor from 1 Jan 2027, and Budget 2027 prep.
- [What Does a Corporate Secretary Do in Singapore?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/corporate-secretary-singapore-what-they-do): A corporate secretary is a statutory officer every Singapore company must appoint within 6 months of incorporation under Section 171 of the Companies Act.
- [GST InvoiceNow Singapore: 2026 Rollout & Founder Action Plan](https://karman.com.sg/blog/gst-invoicenow-singapore-2026): From 1 April 2026, newly GST-registered companies in Singapore must send invoice data to IRAS through InvoiceNow, Singapore's Peppol e-invoicing network.
- [How to Close a Company in Singapore: Step-by-Step Guide 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/how-to-close-company-singapore): A Singapore company can be closed by striking off, the simplest route for companies with no debts or assets, or by members' voluntary winding up when a solvent company has assets to distribute.
- [Penalties for Late Filing in Singapore: ACRA, IRAS, GST & CPF (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/penalties-late-filing-singapore): Late filing in Singapore triggers automated penalties: ACRA fines for late Annual Returns, IRAS surcharges for late ECI and Form C-S, backdated GST registration and penalties for missing the S$1 million threshold, and late-payment interest on CPF contributions due by the 14th of each month.
- [Registered Office Address Singapore: Rules & Options (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/registered-office-address-singapore): Every Singapore company must have a physical registered office address in Singapore from incorporation, where statutory notices can be served. Since 20 October 2026 there is no minimum public opening-hours rule, but company records must be available for inspection on reasonable notice for at least two hours each business day.
- [Singapore Company Annual Compliance Checklist (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-annual-compliance-checklist): A Singapore Pte Ltd must each year file its Annual Return with ACRA, hold or dispense with an AGM, file ECI within 3 months of financial year-end and Form C-S or Form C by 30 November, submit IR8A by 1 March, pay CPF by the 14th of each month, and file GST returns quarterly if registered.
- [Singapore Company Constitution Guide (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-constitution-guide): A Singapore company constitution is the rulebook lodged with ACRA that governs share issues and transfers, director appointments, decision-making and disputes.
- [Singapore Payroll Guide for Employers (2026): CPF, SDL, IR8A](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-payroll-guide-employers): Singapore employers must pay CPF for citizen and PR employees by the 14th of the following month, pay the Skills Development Levy for all employees, issue itemised payslips, file IR8A by 1 March, file IR21 when foreign employees leave, and follow the Employment Act on leave and notice.
- [When Does Your Singapore Company Need to Register for GST?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/when-to-register-gst-singapore): A Singapore company must register for GST when taxable turnover exceeded S$1 million in the past calendar year, or is expected to exceed S$1 million in the next 12 months.

## Guides: Visas & relocation
- [How to Get Singapore PR as an Indian Professional or Founder (2026): Eligibility, Process and Status Check](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-pr-for-indians-2026): Who can apply (EP/S Pass holders need no sponsor), S$100 fee, ICA 6-month processing, status checks via MyICA, completion fees and National Service for sons.
- [COMPASS 2026 Update: New EP Salary & Renewal Rules for Founders](https://karman.com.sg/blog/compass-framework-2026-ep-renewal): From 1 July 2026, COMPASS scoring applies to Employment Pass renewals as well as new applications, and the minimum qualifying salary is S$5,600 a month (S$6,000 from 1 Jan 2027; S$6,200 for financial services).
- [Relocating Your Business from UAE to Singapore](https://karman.com.sg/blog/relocating-business-uae-to-singapore): Businesses relocating from the UAE to Singapore usually incorporate a new Singapore Pte Ltd, transfer contracts and assets, and build genuine Singapore substance.
- [Singapore Employment Pass for Company Directors](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-employment-pass-company-director): Foreign founders can get a Singapore Employment Pass as a director of their own company by incorporating first, paying a salary that meets the MOM minimum (S$5,600 a month, S$6,000 from 1 Jan 2027, higher for older applicants) and scoring at least 40 COMPASS points.
- [Singapore EntrePass for Startup Founders: Complete 2026 Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-entrepass-startup-founders): The Singapore EntrePass lets a foreign founder relocate and run their own innovative company without an employer sponsor or minimum salary.

## Guides: India founders
- [Becoming an NRI in Singapore: Tax Benefits, EP, and What It Actually Costs (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/becoming-nri-singapore-tax-ep-costs): An Indian founder becomes an NRI for tax purposes mainly by spending fewer than 182 days in India in a financial year.
- [FEMA for a Singapore Company: Every Question Answered (Indian Founders, 2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/fema-india-singapore-company-all-questions): Indian residents fund a Singapore company under FEMA through LRS (individuals, up to USD 250,000 per financial year) or ODI (Indian companies).
- [FEMA and RBI Compliance for Indian Founders with a Singapore Company](https://karman.com.sg/blog/fema-rbi-compliance-indian-founders-singapore): Indian founders who own a Singapore company must comply with FEMA's Overseas Investment Rules 2022: invest via LRS or ODI, report share allotments and transfers, file the Annual Performance Report by 31 December each year, and avoid prohibited round-tripping structures.
- [GST Blocked Working Capital? How Indian Exporters Free Their Cash Using Singapore](https://karman.com.sg/blog/gst-blocked-working-capital-singapore-solution): Indian exporters affected by GST's inverted duty structure often wait months for refunds.
- [India-Singapore DTAA: Complete Business Guide (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/india-singapore-dtaa-business-guide): The India-Singapore DTAA reduces withholding tax on cross-border dividends, interest, royalties and fees for technical services.
- [How to Pay Yourself from a Singapore Company as an India Resident (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/pay-yourself-singapore-company-india-resident): If you remain an Indian tax resident, salary, dividends or director's fees from your Singapore company are taxable in India on your worldwide income, with DTAA credit for Singapore tax.
- [Reverse Flip from Singapore to India: Tax, Process, and Timing Guide (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/reverse-flip-india-singapore-guide): A reverse flip moves a startup's holding company from Singapore (or Delaware) back to India, usually ahead of a domestic NSE or BSE IPO.
- [The "Reverse Flip": When US Startups Should Move Their IP and Holding Company to Singapore](https://karman.com.sg/blog/reverse-flip-us-startup-ip-singapore): Moving a US C-Corp's IP and holding company to Singapore is rarely worthwhile.

- [Singapore Incorporation for Indian Founders (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-indian-founders): Indian founders can incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd remotely in 1-3 business days with a nominee director.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Founders: 40+ FAQs Answered (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-india-complete-faq): Indian citizens can own 100% of a Singapore Pte Ltd and incorporate remotely with a nominee director.
- [Cost to Set Up a Singapore Company from India (2026 Full Breakdown)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-india-costs-2026): An Indian founder's Singapore company costs cover incorporation, a nominee director, company secretary and registered address in Year 1, plus accounting and tax filing.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Agricultural Commodity Traders: GTP, DTAA, and Trade Finance (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-agri-commodity-traders): Indian agricultural commodity traders use a Singapore company to sit alongside global trading houses, access cheaper trade finance, and hold buyer relationships, while the Indian entity handles origination and logistics.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Chemical Exporters: DTAA, GTP, and Transfer Pricing Guide (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-chemical-exporters): Indian chemical exporters use a Singapore company as the international sales and trading entity while manufacturing stays in India.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Crypto and Web3 Founders: MAS, Zero CGT, and Regulatory Clarity (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-crypto-web3): Indian crypto and Web3 founders move to Singapore because India taxes virtual digital asset profits at a flat 30% plus 1% TDS, while Singapore has no capital gains tax.
- [Singapore Company for Indian D2C and E-Commerce Brands: Amazon, Shopify, Stripe (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-ecommerce-d2c): Indian D2C and e-commerce brands use a Singapore company to access Stripe and Shopify Payments, sell internationally on Amazon, act as importer of record, and hold multi-currency revenue.
- [Singapore Company for Indian EdTech Founders: International Revenue, VC Fundraising, and ESOP (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-edtech-founders): Indian EdTech founders use a Singapore company to collect international student revenue, hold course IP, raise from international VCs and expand into Southeast Asia.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Engineering Goods Exporters and Manufacturers (2026 Guide)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-engineering-goods-exporters): Indian engineering goods exporters use a Singapore company as the international contracting and trading entity for buyers in Germany, Japan, Korea and the US, while manufacturing and certifications stay in India.
- [Singapore Company for Indian IT Services and Consulting Firms (2026 Guide)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-it-services): Indian IT services firms use a Singapore company as the international contracting entity to bill US, UK and EU clients in foreign currency, reduce permanent establishment risk, hold software IP and relocate key leaders on Employment Passes.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Logistics Companies: ASEAN Regional Hub and Expansion (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-logistics-companies): Indian logistics companies use a Singapore Pte Ltd as their ASEAN regional hub, holding subsidiaries in each country and running regional management and treasury.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Media Companies and Content Creators: International Revenue (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-media-content-creators): Indian creators and media companies use a Singapore company to receive international YouTube, sponsorship and licensing revenue, hold content IP and co-produce with global OTT platforms.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Pharma and API Exporters (2026 Guide)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-pharma-exporters): Indian pharma and API exporters use a Singapore company as the international contracting and trading entity for buyers in the US, EU and Middle East, while USFDA and EU GMP manufacturing stays in India.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Professional Services Firms: International Clients and Tax (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-professional-services): Indian CA firms, lawyers, consultants, architects and engineers use a Singapore company to contract with international clients, bill in USD and serve ASEAN and Middle East markets.
- [Singapore Company for Indian Textile and Trading Exporters (2026 Guide)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-indian-textile-trading-exporters): Indian textile mills, garment exporters and traders use a Singapore Pte Ltd to hold buyer contracts, collect USD, EUR and GBP faster, release GST-blocked working capital and access cheaper trade finance.
- [Singapore Flip Structure for Indian Startups: Complete 2026 Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-flip-structure-indian-startups): A Singapore flip moves an Indian startup's holding company to Singapore so a Singapore Pte Ltd owns the Indian operating company.
- [Singapore Holding Company for Indian Family Businesses (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-holding-company-indian-family-business): Indian family businesses use a Singapore holding company for international expansion, wealth protection and succession planning.
- [Singapore Holding Company for Indian Real Estate Developers: Overseas Assets and FSIE (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-holding-company-indian-real-estate): Indian real estate developers and families use a Singapore holding company to own overseas property SPVs in the UK, Dubai, the US and Asia.
- [Nominee Director for Indian Founders: Cost, Risks, and How It Works (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-nominee-director-india-guide): Indian founders based in India without a Singapore pass need a nominee director to meet the resident director rule.
- [How Indian Textile Exporters Legally Save Tax Using a Singapore Company (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-tax-savings-indian-textile-exporters): Indian textile exporters can legally reduce tax by routing export sales through a Singapore subsidiary taxed at 17% (lower in its first three years) instead of India's 25-30%.
- [Singapore Trading Company for Indian Exporters and Importers (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-trading-company-indian-exporter): Indian exporters and importers use a Singapore trading company to invoice overseas buyers, hold foreign currency revenue, contract under Singapore law and access cheaper trade finance.

## Guides: VCC, funds & family offices
- [Setting Up a Family Office in Singapore: MAS Requirements, 13O/13U & 2026 Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/family-office-singapore-setup-guide): To set up a family office in Singapore, families usually incorporate a Pte Ltd or VCC, rely on the single family office licensing exemption, and apply for the 13O or 13U fund tax incentive, which require minimum AUM, local spending and Singapore-based investment professionals.
- [How Gulf Family Offices Are Using Singapore VCCs](https://karman.com.sg/blog/gulf-family-offices-singapore-vcc): Gulf family offices are increasingly using Singapore VCCs alongside or instead of DIFC, ADGM or Cayman vehicles, attracted by MAS regulation, sub-fund segregation, 13O/13U tax incentives and access to Asian markets.
- [How to Incorporate a VCC in Singapore (2026 Guide)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/how-to-incorporate-vcc-singapore): To incorporate a Singapore VCC, appoint a MAS-regulated fund manager, choose a standalone or umbrella structure, draft a tailored constitution, appoint the mandatory service providers, file with ACRA through a Registered Filing Agent, and then apply for the 13O or 13U tax incentive.
- [MAS VCC Thematic Review 2025: What Fund Managers Must Fix Now](https://karman.com.sg/blog/mas-vcc-thematic-review-2025): MAS Circular IID 04/2025 found widespread VCC compliance gaps in AML/CFT controls, custody arrangements, sub-fund asset segregation, ACRA filings and 13O/13U incentive conditions.
- [Re-domicile a Cayman Fund to Singapore VCC](https://karman.com.sg/blog/redomicile-cayman-fund-to-singapore-vcc): A Cayman fund can transfer to Singapore as a VCC by re-domiciliation (continuation) without being wound up, keeping its legal identity, assets and investor relationships.
- [Redomiciling a DIFC or ADGM Fund to a Singapore VCC: Complete Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/redomicile-difc-adgm-fund-to-singapore-vcc): A DIFC or ADGM fund cannot redomicile directly into a Singapore VCC the way a Cayman fund can.
- [Saudi Family Offices and Singapore VCCs: A 2026 Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/saudi-family-offices-singapore-vcc): Saudi families diversifying wealth under Vision 2030 increasingly use a Singapore VCC as their family office vehicle.
- [MAS Fund Management License Singapore: CMS, RFMC, VCC & 13O/13U Guide 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-fund-management-license-mas): Managing third-party money in Singapore requires a MAS Capital Markets Services licence for fund management or an exemption.
- [Singapore VCC for US Fund Managers: Check-the-Box, FinCEN AML Rule, and Marketing to US LPs in 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vcc-us-fund-managers-fincen-aml): US emerging managers increasingly use a Singapore VCC for Asia-focused funds.
- [Singapore VCC vs Mauritius GBC: Which India Fund Vehicle Wins in 2026?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vcc-vs-mauritius-gbc-india-funds): For new India-focused funds in 2026, the Singapore VCC is the default and the Mauritius GBC is largely a legacy structure.
- [Single vs Multi-Family Office Singapore: Structure, Cost & Which to Choose 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/single-vs-multi-family-office-singapore): A Single Family Office manages only one family's wealth and is exempt from MAS fund management licensing; a Multi-Family Office serves several unrelated families and needs a CMS licence.
- [Umbrella VCC vs Standalone VCC Singapore](https://karman.com.sg/blog/umbrella-vcc-vs-standalone-singapore): Choose a standalone VCC for a single fund strategy with one investor class; choose an umbrella VCC if you plan multiple strategies, vintages or investor groups, since sub-funds can be added later by resolution with segregated assets and liabilities.
- [VCC Singapore: Complete Guide for Fund Managers](https://karman.com.sg/blog/variable-capital-company-singapore-vcc): A Variable Capital Company (VCC) is Singapore's corporate structure for investment funds, introduced in January 2020.
- [Section 13O and 13U Tax Incentives for Singapore VCCs: 2025 Complete Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/vcc-13o-13u-tax-incentives-singapore): Sections 13O and 13U of Singapore's Income Tax Act exempt specified income from designated investments of qualifying funds, including VCCs.
- [VCC Annual Compliance Singapore: What to File, When, and With Whom](https://karman.com.sg/blog/vcc-annual-compliance-singapore): A Singapore VCC must file its Annual Return with ACRA within 7 months of financial year-end, hold an AGM within 6 months unless dispensed with, file audited financial statements and tax returns, and rely on its fund manager to meet MAS obligations.
- [VCC Compliance Requirements Singapore: Complete Checklist (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/vcc-compliance-requirements-singapore): A Singapore VCC carries more compliance than a Pte Ltd, spanning ACRA corporate filings, MAS regulatory status of the fund manager, IRAS tax filings and 13O/13U declarations, fund administration and NAV calculation, and AML/CFT controls.
- [VCC for Family Offices in Singapore (2025 Guide)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/vcc-family-office-singapore-2025): Family offices use a Singapore VCC to combine sub-fund segregation, a private register of members, 13O/13U tax exemptions and multi-generational planning.
- [VCC Fund Administration Singapore: Every Mandatory Service Provider Explained](https://karman.com.sg/blog/vcc-fund-administration-singapore): A Singapore VCC needs a mandated set of service providers: a MAS-licensed or exempt fund manager, a company secretary, an auditor, a fund administrator, a custodian or depositary where required, and AML/CFT compliance support.
- [VCC Setup Cost in Singapore: Full 2026 Breakdown](https://karman.com.sg/blog/vcc-setup-cost-singapore-2026): The cost of a Singapore VCC is driven far more by service providers than by government fees: legal documentation, fund manager arrangements, fund administration, audit and company secretary.
- [Singapore VCC vs Cayman Islands Fund: Which Structure is Right for You? (2025)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/vcc-singapore-vs-cayman-islands): Choose a Singapore VCC for Asia-focused funds that benefit from Singapore's 100+ tax treaties, onshore substance and MAS regulation.
- [Why the Singapore VCC Is the Best Fund Vehicle in Asia (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/why-vcc-good-vehicle-for-funds-singapore): The Singapore VCC is a leading fund vehicle in Asia because it combines variable capital (issue and redeem at NAV), umbrella sub-fund segregation, near-zero tax under 13O/13U, access to Singapore's treaty network, a private register of members and MAS regulatory credibility.

## Guides: Comparisons
- [EntrePass vs Employment Pass Singapore: Which Visa for Founders in 2026?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/entrepass-vs-employment-pass-singapore): Choose the Employment Pass if your Singapore company can pay you at least S$5,600 a month (S$6,000 from 1 Jan 2027; S$6,200 in financial services) and you can pass COMPASS.
- [India vs Singapore Tax for Founders: Full Comparison 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/india-vs-singapore-tax-founders): Singapore taxes founders far less than India: corporate tax of 17% headline (4-8% effective for new companies) versus 25-30% in India, no capital gains tax versus 10-20%, and a top personal rate of 22% versus 30%.
- [Singapore Pte Ltd vs Indian Private Limited: Which Should You Set Up? (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-pte-ltd-vs-indian-private-limited): Choose an Indian Private Limited if you serve Indian customers with domestic operations.
- [Singapore Pte Ltd vs Sole Proprietorship vs LLP](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-pte-ltd-vs-sole-proprietor-llp): For almost every founder, a Singapore Pte Ltd is the right structure: limited liability, a lower corporate tax rate with startup exemptions, the ability to raise investment and greater credibility.
- [Singapore Subsidiary vs Branch vs Representative Office (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-subsidiary-vs-branch-office): A foreign company entering Singapore can set up a subsidiary (a separate Pte Ltd), a branch (an extension of the parent) or a representative office (a temporary, non-commercial liaison office).
- [Singapore vs Cayman vs Dubai for US Founders Going Offshore in 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-cayman-vs-dubai-us-founders-2026): For US founders going offshore in 2026, Singapore suits Asia-focused operating companies, Cayman remains the default for LP fund vehicles, and Dubai suits founders seeking 0% personal tax and Middle East markets.
- [Singapore Pte Ltd vs Delaware C-Corp: Founder's Decision Guide 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-delaware-c-corp-2026): Incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd if your customers are global and you are not committed to a US raise - it minimises tax and friction.
- [Singapore vs Delaware for Indian Startups: Which Holding Company in 2026?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-delaware-indian-startups): Indian founders should choose a Delaware C-Corp when customers and investors are mainly in the US, and a Singapore Pte Ltd when operations and customers are in India, ASEAN or the Middle East.
- [Singapore vs Dubai for Company Incorporation: 2025 Comparison](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-dubai-company-incorporation): Choose Dubai for MENA-focused trading, zero personal income tax and lifestyle relocation.
- [Singapore vs Dubai for Indian Founders: Tax, Credibility, and Cost Compared (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-dubai-indian-founders): Indian founders should choose Dubai for 0% personal income tax, lifestyle relocation and Middle East re-export trade, and Singapore for raising institutional VC or private equity, the India-Singapore DTAA and stronger credibility.
- [Singapore vs GIFT City for Indian Founders and Fund Managers (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-gift-city-indian-founders): Choose Singapore for international VC fundraising and global LPs; choose GIFT City for India-focused funds with mainly Indian or NRI investors, where its 100% tax holiday for 10 of 15 years is attractive.
- [Singapore vs Hong Kong 2026: Which Is Better for Founders Now?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-hong-kong-2026): For most founders in 2026, Singapore is the default choice over Hong Kong because of easier banking, lower political risk and strong talent visas.
- [Singapore vs Hong Kong for Indian Founders: Which Asian Base in 2026?](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-hong-kong-indian-founders): Most Indian founders should choose Singapore over Hong Kong for its comprehensive India-Singapore DTAA, easier banking and Southeast Asia access.
- [Singapore vs Malaysia: Which Country to Incorporate In? (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-vs-malaysia-company-incorporation): Choose Singapore if you are raising VC funding, serving international customers or need strong banking and capital mobility.

## Guides: US founders & trade
- [De Minimis Is Gone: How US E-commerce Brands Should Restructure Through Singapore in 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/de-minimis-eliminated-us-ecommerce-singapore): The US$800 de minimis exemption ended on 24 February 2026, so every parcel entering the US now needs formal entry and duty.
- [FBAR + Form 8938 for US Founders With a Singapore Pte Ltd: 2026 Compliance Checklist](https://karman.com.sg/blog/fbar-form-8938-us-founders-singapore-pte-ltd): Most US founders with a Singapore Pte Ltd must file both an FBAR (FinCEN 114) and Form 8938 (FATCA).
- [Form 5471 for Singapore Pte Ltd Owners: Complete 2026 Filing Guide](https://karman.com.sg/blog/form-5471-singapore-pte-ltd-2026): US persons who own or control a Singapore Pte Ltd almost always file Form 5471 with their US tax return.
- [GILTI Is Dead, Long Live NCTI: What US Owners of Singapore Companies Owe in 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/gilti-ncti-us-owners-singapore-companies-2026): For tax years beginning after 31 December 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act replaced GILTI with NCTI, which generally increases US tax for US persons owning 10% or more of a Singapore Pte Ltd that is a controlled foreign corporation.
- [What the Section 301 Investigation on Singapore Means for US Founders With Singapore Operations](https://karman.com.sg/blog/section-301-investigation-singapore-us-founders): USTR opened a Section 301 investigation into Singapore on 11 March 2026, focused largely on transshipment of China-origin goods.
- [Singapore Incorporation for US Founders (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-company-incorporation-us-founders): US founders can incorporate a Singapore Pte Ltd remotely, but the US taxes citizens and green card holders on worldwide income and there is no comprehensive US-Singapore tax treaty.
- [Singapore Holding Company for US-Owned SaaS: FDDEI, NCTI, and the New 14% Sweet Spot](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-holding-company-us-saas-fddei-ncti): From 2026, OBBBA renamed FDII to FDDEI (an effective US rate around 14% on foreign-derived income) and replaced GILTI with NCTI.
- [Trump's 15% Tariff and Your Singapore Supply Chain: First Sale Rule, FTZs, and What Actually Works in 2026](https://karman.com.sg/blog/trump-tariffs-singapore-supply-chain-first-sale-fts): US importers with supply chains running through Singapore can legally reduce duty using the First Sale for Export rule, Foreign Trade Zones, bonded warehouses and correct HTS classification.
- [US Tariffs and Singapore Incorporation: What Founders Need to Know](https://karman.com.sg/blog/us-tariffs-singapore-company-incorporation): Incorporating in Singapore is not a tariff shortcut.

## Guides: Other guides
- [Singapore Pte Ltd: How to Pay Yourself - Salary vs Dividend (2026)](https://karman.com.sg/blog/pay-yourself-singapore-pte-ltd): Singapore founders usually pay themselves through a mix of salary and dividends.
- [Singapore Political Stability & Business Continuity](https://karman.com.sg/blog/singapore-political-stability-business-continuity): Singapore's political stability, consistent governance and rule of law reduce the risk that legal, regulatory or banking conditions change suddenly.
